title: Frog Chorus Intensity After Rain
dataSources: Bird acoustic detections (`birdnet:detection`), wildlife-camera visits (`wildlifecam:visit`), nest-box state (`nestbox:event`), frog-call activity (`frogcall:detection`), and pollinator counts (`pollinator:count`).
app: Wildlife telemetry from BirdNET, trail and feeder cameras, nest-box sensors, frog-call detectors, and pollinator counters streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted imports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=frogcall:detection
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(call_intensity) as avg_call_intensity avg(rain_mm) as avg_rain_mm by _time
| sort - _time
description: Compares daily frog-call intensity with rainfall totals to show when wet weather wakes the chorus up.
value: It is a simple but satisfying way to connect backyard acoustics with the conditions that trigger amphibian activity.
implementation: Stream frog-call detector intensity and local rainfall from the same site or a nearby weather station.
visualization: Dual-axis line chart of frog-call intensity and rainfall by day.
grandmaExplanation: It logs how much the frog chorus picks up after rainy weather.
